About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

Base designs its own hardware, builds it in its own factory, installs it at homes, and sells the power. That vertical integration is our advantage, and it means the suppliers we choose and the deals we strike directly shape our cost and speed.

As a GSM Intern, you will own sourcing for a set of assigned parts, run the RFQ process end to end, and negotiate cost and terms directly with suppliers.

This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to source, suppliers to negotiate with, and quotes that carry real weight in our build cost. The work sits between Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Finance, and suits someone who thinks in systems, is comfortable acting on incomplete information, and likes building durable, repeatable sourcing processes.

What You’ll Do

- Own sourcing for a set of assigned parts: build and run RFQs, compare supplier quotes on cost, lead time, and capacity, and make the call on award.

- Negotiate price, payment terms, and lead time directly with suppliers, and track savings against the prior baseline.

- Build supplier cost models — bottoms-up where you can — so you can tell a fair quote from a padded one.

- Support qualification of new suppliers and second sources for critical components: gather quotes, samples, and capability data for the team’s decision.

- Track supplier performance — cost, delivery, and quality — and flag risk before it hits the production line.

What You’ll Bring

- Working toward a degree in supply chain, industrial engineering, operations, mechanical engineering, business, or another quantitative field — or on a comparable path.

- Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort working with large, messy datasets. SQL, Python, or scripting is a plus.

- Genuine interest in how physical products get built. Exposure to an MRP or ERP system (Odoo, SAP, NetSuite) is a plus, not a requirement.

- Clear, direct written communication — you will send RFQs, quote comparisons, and escalations to suppliers and internal teams.

- Bias to action and follow-through. You close loops without being asked twice.

- Available to work in person in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship.

About the Team

Global Supply Management owns every part that goes into a Base battery and its associated systems. This includes sourcing, planning, and getting it to the line on time. We are ramping in-house manufacturing of our own battery product while qualifying second sources for critical components, which means the plan changes often and the cost of being wrong is a stopped line. Sourcing is where that pressure lands first: the team decides who we buy from and on what terms, and builds the leverage and systems that make those calls repeatable.

Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.

Our Values

- First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

- Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

- Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

- Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

- Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

- Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

- Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

Do the best work of your life at Base.

The Team

The Generalist Robot Learning (GRL) team in the Robotics division is looking for research interns for Summer 2027. We are advancing core methods in 3D perception, representation learning, and world modeling. These methods enable robots to understand, reconstruct, simulate, and interact with the world across diverse environments and sensor modalities. Our work spans:

- 3D and Multi-Modal Foundation Models

- Simulation and Co-Training (Sim2Real, Real2Sim, Real2Sim2Real)

- World Models (Action-Conditioned World Models, World Action Models, 3D World Models)

Our mission is to develop generalizable, data-driven representations and world models that bridge computer vision, graphics, simulation, and robotics. About the Role

OpenGov is looking for Product Engineer Interns who are eager to learn what it means to own a product — from customer discovery through delivery. This internship is built around a new kind of role born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required multiple specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, talk to customers, make the right call in ambiguous situations, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers learn to do — and this internship is where that journey starts.

This role is first and foremost about developing product thinking — not becoming a developer. The best interns will be the ones who grow genuinely curious about customers: who they are, what they actually need, and what outcomes depend on solving their problems. The engineering side — using AI-native tooling to write code, build interfaces — is a skill you will be introduced to and encouraged to develop. It is a career accelerator, not a day-one requirement.

If you have a background or strong interest in product management, UX design, engineering, or some combination — and you want real ownership of a problem rather than a slide deck — this internship is for you.

"Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there.

The 10-week internship will run from June 7, 2027 through August 13, 2027.

What You'll Work On

- A scoped product problem: a defined set of customers, problems, and outcomes — sized for a 10–12 week engagement with real impact.

- Customer discovery: you will conduct or observe customer conversations and translate what you learn into product decisions.

- User experience flows: you will define interaction patterns within an existing design system and validate them with users.

- AI-assisted delivery: using AI-native tooling, you will move from intent to spec to working prototype — supported by your team, but accountable for the output.

- Metrics: you will define what success looks like for your area and track it throughout the internship.

How AI Works in This Role

AI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and designers have historically spent their time on. As an intern, you will be hands-on with these tools from day one:

- Spec writing: AI drafts the first spec from your intent statement. You learn to review, sharpen, and own what gets built.

- UX design: AI generates mockups from the design system based on your flow definitions. You make the product decisions within it.

- Research synthesis: AI clusters and themes interview notes and support data. You interpret what it means and make the call.

- Release content: AI generates release notes and enablement materials from shipped features. You review and refine them.

- Test coverage: AI generates test cases from acceptance criteria. You learn to write criteria precise enough to verify.

What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job — and what you will be learning.

Key Responsibilities

- Participate in customer discovery conversations; synthesize what you hear into defensible product decisions.

- Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the existing design system.

- Write intent documents that AI tooling can execute against; review AI-generated specs for accuracy and completeness.

- Partner with your engineering and product mentor to resolve ambiguity in real time during the development cycle.

- Track adoption and usage metrics for your scoped area; use them to drive iteration.

- Present your product area and findings in a final intern showcase — covering the customer problem, what you built, and what you would do next.

- Surface gaps, risks, and unanswered questions proactively; don't wait to be asked.

Qualifications & What We're Looking For

- Currently pursuing a degree in computer science, information systems, product design, HCI, business, or a closely adjacent field — or equivalent self-directed experience.

- Genuine curiosity about customers and why products succeed or fail; you find yourself asking "who is this for and does it actually solve their problem?"

- Strong written communication: you can articulate a product decision clearly enough that an engineer and a designer walk away aligned.

- Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you make reasonable decisions with incomplete information rather than waiting for certainty.

- Willingness to grow into code fluency using AI-native tooling — you don't need to arrive as a developer, but you must be willing to get there.

- Prior exposure to product management, UX design, software development, or customer research is a plus — in any form (coursework, projects, prior internships, side work).

- Make AI tools for others. You build a skill, a tool, or an agent workflow that your team keeps using after your internship ends.

- Measure, don't guess. You write evals and tests so you can prove that your AI-powered work is good.

- You have good fundamentals. You can write clean code, you are familiar with design patterns, and you understand data structures, APIs, and testing.

- You have built things outside of class. Side projects, hackathons, open source, and freelance work all count.

- You have applied AI, not only chatted with it. What have you built? Tell us about an app on an LLM API, a custom agent or MCP server, a boring task you automated end to end, or a simple eval you used to compare prompts or models.

- You stay curious and sceptical. You ask why the AI gave an answer, and you check it before you trust it.

- You learn fast. You are excited to learn new things. You are comfortable when you do not know something yet, and you ask good questions.

Show Us What You Built with AI

Tell us about:

- The coolest one: the thing you are most proud of, or the thing that made people say "wait, how?"

- Or the hardest one: the thing that broke many times before it worked.

- The problem: what you wanted to solve, and why it mattered to you.

- What you built: what you built, compared to what the AI did.

- What broke: where the AI failed, and how you found and fixed the problem.

- The result: a link to a repo, a demo, a video, or a write-up. A result that works with rough edges is better than slides that look polished.

- Agents: you built an agent that uses tools, keeps memory, or runs many steps without a human.

- Evals: you wrote evals or tests to measure whether your AI output improved.

- Real users: you shipped something that people other than you actually use.

- Cloud: you deployed your project to a cloud platform.

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.

Role Overview

REGENT's Energy Storage System team is working on one of the most foundational questions behind our Seagliders: how do we store and deliver the energy that gets them across the water, safely and efficiently, mission after mission. As our ESS Intern, you'll dig directly into that question — splitting your time between hands-on test support, battery characterization, and simulation work that spans our Squire and Viceroy programs. You'll help the team understand how individual cells and full packs actually behave under real conditions, how they should be integrated into our platforms, and how to optimally design the high voltage vehicle architecture. This isn't a narrow, single-task internship — it's a genuinely broad technical role with real scope behind it, built for someone who wants to learn by doing.

You'll sit within our Hardware Engineering group, working closely with the Electrical Systems and Mechanical teams, where precision and curiosity go hand in hand. The team moves fast and expects you to pick up REGENT-specific tools and architectures quickly, but once you're oriented, you'll be trusted to run with real analysis and contribute findings that shape how we think about battery integration going forward.

If you're a student with strong engineering fundamentals who gets energized by ambiguity, hands-on testing, and the chance to help define how next-generation electric watercraft get their power, this is a place where you'll do work that matters from day one.

What You'll Do

- Characterize Battery Packs: You'll run tests on battery packs to understand how they perform under the conditions our Seagliders actually face. Your findings will directly inform how the team evaluates viable energy storage options.

- Support Paladin Test Operations: You'll get hands-on with test support and battery servicing, working alongside engineers who rely on accurate, well-documented testing to move programs forward. This is where you'll build real intuition for how packs behave outside of a datasheet.

- Model Mission-Profile Performance: Using Python or MATLAB, you'll build simulations that show how battery performance holds up across different mission profiles. This work helps the team make informed tradeoffs long before hardware decisions are finalized.

- Contribute to Integration Documentation: You'll help document how battery systems integrate into REGENT's high voltage architecture across platforms. Clear, thorough documentation here keeps the whole team moving faster.

- Own Energy Budgets and Trade Studies: You'll build and refine energy budgets and trade studies in Excel that compare options across cost, performance, and integration complexity. These studies feed directly into engineering decisions on the program.

- Track Cell and Pack Data: You'll help monitor pack-specific characteristics during testing, keeping an eye on the details that matter for performance and safety. Good data here is the foundation for everything else the team builds on top of it.

What You'll Bring

- Strong Engineering Fundamentals: You're currently a senior or graduate student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or chemical engineering. You come in with the core fundamentals already in place, ready to apply them from week one.

- Li-ion Battery Knowledge: You understand the basics of lithium-ion systems — capacity, C-rate, state of charge, internal resistance, voltage curves, and series/parallel configurations. This foundation is essential to the work you'll be doing all summer.

- Analytical Toolkit: You're proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis and modeling, and you're comfortable building energy budgets and trade studies in Excel. A significant part of this role involves analyzing battery performance across different mission profiles.

- Comfort With Ambiguity: You're self-directed and don't need every task spelled out to make meaningful progress. You can take a loosely defined problem and figure out how to move it forward.

- Clear Communication: You can explain your findings and tradeoffs to engineers in a way that's useful and easy to act on. Translating technical analysis into clear takeaways is a core part of this role.

- CAD Familiarity, A Plus: Experience with a 3D CAD tool like SolidWorks, Fusion, or Creo, along with the ability to produce clear drawings, would help you move quickly and bridge gaps between electrical and mechanical work.

- Pack and Simulation Experience, A Plus: Any exposure to pack-level design work — cell selection, BMS architecture, busbars, thermal management — or to battery simulation tools like PyBaMM, Simulink/Simscape Battery, or COMSOL will help you hit the ground running.

Who We're Looking For

- Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

- Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

- Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.
